nodes.description: TBCK forms a heterotrimer with PPP1R21 and FERRY3/C12orf4 that acts as a specific GTPase-activating protein for RAB5, and is a subunit of the wider five-subunit FERRY complex (with CRYZL1 and GATD1) that couples early endosomes to mRNA for peripheral local translation. Loss of the GAP leaves RAB5 constitutively GTP-bound. Despite the gene name, TBCK's N-terminal kinase-like domain is a catalytically inactive class I pseudokinase lacking the VAIK, HRD and DFG motifs and nucleotide binding, so the disease-relevant activity resides in the central TBC/Rab-GAP domain.
